entries.name: @bsv/402-pay
entries.summary: Adds an exact-tarball Vite and esbuild contract for the browser-safe client entry point, including a bundle-size ratchet and an assertion that server exports never leak into browser consumers. Retains the hash-pinned pre-uniformization Open BSV License version 4 grant as a scoped continuity notice. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name. Binds BRC-121 pricing and internalization to the transaction declared by the BRC-95 Atomic BEEF subject, removes unrelated included branches, rejects trailing bytes and non-atomic envelopes, and requires affirmative wallet acceptance before serving paid content. Adds independent bounded atomic transaction replay claims so conforming BRC-100 wallets that omit the non-public isMerge detail cannot authorize duplicate access, preserves actual overpayments in middleware receipts, uses fixed bounded wallet descriptions, makes diagnostics opt-in, and returns an unchallenged 503 after ambiguous wallet or replay-store failures to avoid inducing a second spend. Aligns the development-only Vitest runner and V8 coverage provider at 4.1.11.
entries.migration: Custom clients must send a strictly framed BRC-95 Atomic BEEF envelope whose subject is the payment transaction; plain BEEF is no longer accepted. Legacy Atomic BEEF containing unrelated branches remains compatible because the server reduces it to the declared subject and dependency closure. The default replay store is bounded and process-local; production services with more than one serving process or node must inject the same durable atomic PaymentReplayStore everywhere. Low-level validators should retain one wallet object or pass an explicit store. Applications that relied on implicit console diagnostics must supply the optional structured logger. Treat an unchallenged 503 after payment submission as ambiguous and reconcile the transaction before requesting another payment. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package.

entries.name: @bsv/air-gap
entries.summary: Bounds BRC-141 decoder state, scanned strings, duplicate tracking, pending mixes, fountain indices, and high-degree work while replacing sparse O(K) index materialization with bounded mapping. Systematic and degree-one frames remain available under pressure and valid wire-v1 payloads retain their bytes.
entries.migration: No migration is required for valid BRC-141 v1 senders or decoders. Malformed, oversized, duplicate-heavy, or adversarial high-degree sessions now fail closed or are evicted within the documented limits instead of consuming unbounded resources.

entries.name: @bsv/amountinator
entries.summary: Validates finite monetary values, normalized nonempty currency codes, integer decimal precision, grouping flags, converter rates, and conversion results, and formats negative sub-unit amounts from their absolute magnitude without losing the sign.
entries.migration: Valid finite inputs retain the public API. Currency identifiers are trimmed and normalized to uppercase; callers that passed non-finite values, empty currencies, coercive options, invalid decimal precision, or non-finite converter results must normalize or reject them before calling because those values now fail closed.

entries.name: @bsv/auth
entries.summary: Adopts the governed strict TypeScript profile and repository-wide zero-warning lint and formatting contract. Snapshots canonical own-data proof fields, dense signature bytes, bodies, protocols, wallet identities, and exact wallet verdicts before asynchronous work; rejects accessor/inherited authority and ambiguous JSON numbers; and retains exact nonce-consumption replay claims. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name.
entries.migration: No valid proof bytes or public API shape changes. Client and server must use the same protocol tuple; security levels 0, 1, and 2 remain supported and select wallet consent policy while the explicit counterparty scopes derivation at every level. Proof and wallet adapters must supply plain own data fields and dense byte arrays; inherited, accessor-backed, sparse, or malformed runtime shapes fail closed. Structured bodies containing non-finite numbers or negative zero must be normalized to an unambiguous wire representation before signing.

entries.name: @bsv/auth-express-middleware
entries.summary: Adds optional final authenticated HTTP response admission after BRC-104 signing, with native synchronous enqueue, one bounded re-signed replacement and deadline/disconnect cancellation. Ordinary response behavior, peer ranges and wire representation are preserved. Existing bounded integration fixtures retain their development-only rate limiter.
entries.migration: No change for ordinary routes. Guarded routes explicitly call guardAuthenticatedResponse after authentication and before sending; acquire the application durable fence, recheck current authorization and targets, and synchronously enqueue under it. Native Node HTTP/1 transport is required without compression/deferred response wrappers. Replacements are complete responses limited to64KiB and must preserve required CORS/capability headers. No production rate-limiting or transport defaults change.

entries.name: @bsv/authsocket
entries.summary: Contains authentication and application callback failures, caps per-socket authentication concurrency, gates every concurrently received first-session event and routing decision on one completed authenticated-connection activation, snapshots strict JSON before signing, serializes real typed arrays portably, and preserves supported signed event JSON exactly. Retains the hash-pinned pre-uniformization Open BSV License version 4 grant as a scoped continuity notice. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name.
entries.migration: No API or wire migration is required for valid JSON events. Existing numeric-key objects under byte-like names are unchanged; typed payment protocols recover historical byte objects at their explicit fields. Outbound non-JSON or ambiguous runtime values, including negative zero, nested undefined, sparse arrays, accessors, hidden/extra properties, and serialization hooks, now fail closed before signing. requestedCertificates is an SDK allowlist, not an application authorization verdict. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package.

entries.name: @bsv/authsocket-client
entries.summary: Contains authentication and application callback failures, caps authentication concurrency, snapshots strict JSON before signing, serializes real typed arrays portably, preserves supported signed event JSON exactly, and ships the complete SDK incorporated-material notice archive with a retained UMD notice banner. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name.
entries.migration: No API or wire migration is required for valid JSON events. Existing numeric-key objects under byte-like names are unchanged; typed payment protocols recover historical byte objects at their explicit fields. Outbound non-JSON or ambiguous runtime values, including negative zero, nested undefined, sparse arrays, accessors, hidden/extra properties, and serialization hooks, now fail closed before signing. The connect event/connected property report Socket.IO transport state, not completed BRC-103 authentication; wait for verified application traffic when local behavior requires a known unpinned server. Distributors who copy the UMD file must keep THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with it.

entries.name: @bsv/btms
entries.summary: Adds TerraTestNet and preserves token settlement and refund transaction bytes across number-array, Uint8Array, and historical numeric-key JSON wallet runtimes. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name. Rejects non-canonical or unsafe token amounts, applies exact checked arithmetic to financial aggregates, and enforces value conservation for custom change strategies.
entries.migration: Existing local, mainnet, testnet, and number-array behavior is unchanged. TTN consumers select networkPreset teratestnet; all consumers should upgrade to @bsv/sdk 2.4.1 or later for byte-boundary compatibility. Valid canonical token amounts remain compatible. Audit historical tokens for signed, exponent, leading-zero, non-positive, or greater-than-9007199254740991 amount fields before rebuilding wallet state; public number-based operations now fail closed when an aggregate cannot be represented exactly.

entries.name: @bsv/btms-permission-module
entries.summary: Requires literal authorization verdicts, bounds authorization state, validates dense signature bytes and safe-integer totals, and binds BTMS signing to an exact canonical BIP143 preimage with no trailing data.
entries.migration: Valid canonical BTMS flows remain compatible. Custom prompts must return literal true, authorization maps may contain at most 1,024 entries, and callers must provide dense signatures, safe exact totals, and canonical preimages; coercive or trailing-byte forms now fail closed.

entries.name: @bsv/ecpm-permission-module
entries.summary: Hardens the BRC-98 ecpm boundary with plain-own-data arguments, exact key, point, protocol, and counterparty validation, immutable configuration snapshots, originator binding, and bounded grant and pending-authorization state.
entries.migration: Valid ecpm requests remain compatible. Authorization callbacks must return literal true; inherited, accessor-backed, malformed, or oversized inputs now fail closed. Hosts must keep grants below 1,024 entries and avoid more than 64 concurrently pending new authorization prompts per module instance.

entries.name: @bsv/chirp
entries.summary: Fixes authenticated CHIRP object uploads: omit explicit Content-Length and Content-Encoding application headers that AuthFetch rejects, while HTTP transport generates the correct length and absent encoding preserves identity bytes. Adds a real mutually authenticated client/server regression that verifies raw object bytes, automatic HTTP framing, object identifiers, caller identity, and successful commit.
entries.migration: No API, codec, object identifier, service schema, or wire-format migration. Use @bsv/chirp 0.1.3 with SDK 2.8.9 or later and Cloud Bucket 0.2.48 or Lite 0.1.45 for authenticated binary uploads, including full 4 MiB chunks. Custom authenticated transports must send the supplied owned byte body unchanged and supply ordinary HTTP framing; Content-Type remains signed through AuthFetch. Earlier service entrypoints do not parse staged binary bytes before authentication and require this service patch. Existing stored objects, sessions, advertisements and leases remain unchanged.

entries.name: @bsv/lch
entries.summary: Hardens the BRC-170 Licensed Content Header implementation with deterministic malformed-input handling, URL-canonical SSRF protection including IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals, bounded DAG composition, authenticated settlement evidence, replay-safe receipts, recovery-safe multipay state, and signed-Offer agreement binding. Removes the endpoint-only quote overload because it cannot authenticate the Asset, Policy, Agreement, seller, or key-delivery terms.
entries.migration: Replace buyer.quote(endpoint, request, issuer, keyGrants) with buyer.quote(verifiedSignedOffer, request, expectedSeller, keyGrants). JavaScript callers that still pass an endpoint string fail before transport I/O. Persist the returned plan and every partial settlement proof, retry with the same funded transaction, and configure a profile-aware agreementEvaluator before completion or recovery. Low-level unverified recovery results must not authorize key storage or content access. DNS endpoints require an address-pinning connector outside trusted browser environments. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md with the package; published BRC-170 remains authoritative if the implementation and standard differ.

entries.name: @bsv/did
entries.summary: Fixes the CommonJS build of the DID key, signature and multibase helpers. The CommonJS build imported @bsv/sdk classes through bundler Node-mode interop, which bound each default import to the whole SDK module, so require() consumers failed at first use with ".default is not a constructor". SDK classes are now imported by name from the SDK barrels; the ESM build, public API and browser bundle size are unchanged.
entries.migration: None. ESM consumers are unaffected.

entries.name: @bsv/did-client
entries.summary: Fixes the CommonJS build so DIDClient can construct SDK lookup, broadcast, PushDrop, transaction and wallet objects. The CommonJS build imported @bsv/sdk classes through bundler Node-mode interop, which bound each default import to the whole SDK module, so require() consumers failed at first use with ".default is not a constructor". SDK classes are now imported by name from the SDK barrels; the ESM build, public API and browser bundle size are unchanged. Raises the @bsv/sdk peer floor from ^2.4.0 to ^2.8.0: the package already requires SDK modules (identity/DIDTokenValidation, wallet/completeBoundAction) that first shipped in 2.8.0, so earlier 2.x SDKs never loaded it.
entries.migration: Use @bsv/sdk 2.8.0 or later (earlier 2.x releases were already incompatible). No API migration is required; ESM consumers are otherwise unaffected.

entries.name: @bsv/fund-wallet
entries.summary: Requires the funding wallet's internalizeAction result to contain accepted: true before reporting a funded transaction as successfully internalized.
entries.migration: No public API migration is required for conforming wallets. Custom WalletInterface adapters must return the literal accepted: true verdict after successful internalization; refusals and malformed or coercive results now throw instead of being reported as success.

entries.name: @bsv/gasp
entries.summary: Validates and correlates every GASP page, outpoint, node, raw transaction, metadata field, requested-input map, and completion result; caps page, graph, metadata and concurrency work; prevents prototype-sensitive records, quadratic replies, stale-watermark advancement, and non-progressing pagination. Retains the positional constructor and v1 wire contract while documenting the parent-availability assumption of the bidirectional push half.
entries.migration: No API or wire migration is required. In bidirectional mode, the receiver must already have the parent of a pushed child, request it during a subsequent synchronization round, or reject the graph because GASP v1 submitNode does not transmit the spentBy parent outpoint. Pull-only operation avoids that assumption. Custom storage and remote adapters must preserve exact request/node binding and bounded responses.

entries.name: @bsv/message-box-client
entries.summary: Raises the @bsv/sdk peer floor from ^2.8.0 to ^2.8.6. SDK 2.8.0 through 2.8.5 derive the recipient key in Brc29RemittanceModule.acceptSettlement without forSelf, so PeerPayClient.acceptPayment() and rejectPayment() terminate with brc29.internalize_failed for every valid incoming payment. SDK 2.8.6 fixes acceptance; this package has no source change.
entries.migration: Install @bsv/sdk 2.8.6 or later alongside this package. No API, BRC100 wire or wallet-data migration. Payments refused on earlier SDKs remain pending in the message box and can be accepted after upgrading.

entries.name: @bsv/overlay
entries.summary: Adds an optional retained-admission history contract and explicit Mongo retention. New opt-in commits preserve bounded immutable identity alongside the existing public receipt; trusted history reads bind applied topic, policy, context and operation after restart without asserting current unspentness or visibility. Legacy submission, receipt bytes and database validators remain unchanged.
entries.migration: None for existing consumers. To retain provenance for new commits, explicitly construct MongoOverlayStorage or MongoAdmissionStorage with retainAdmissionHistory: true. Existing receipts are not rewritten or retroactively certified; history remains unresolved when binding material is absent. Readers must authorize and project private multi-topic results. Disable the option to return to legacy writes; saved metadata remains compatible with legacy receipt readers. No database schema migration or deployment is performed.

entries.name: @bsv/overlay-discovery-services
entries.summary: Advances the packed Overlay runtime dependency for the additive retained-admission history API. Existing package behavior and defaults remain unchanged; history retention is not enabled automatically.
entries.migration: None. The compatible dependency candidate does not change HTTP routes, topic/lookup interfaces, storage selection, or deployment configuration. Publication and deployment remain separate authorized actions.

entries.name: @bsv/overlay-express
entries.summary: Adds optional progressive and resumable live lookup routes with a structural provider companion, exact signed capability selection, bounded raw request parsing, fresh authenticated principals, no-store responses and cancellation. configureOutputLookup reuses the existing authentication session and server capacity. Legacy routes, finite lookup behavior and default startup remain unchanged; retained-admission history remains opt-in. Add an optional root-advertisement final HTTP send companion with current data/control authorization and bounded signed reset replacement.
entries.migration: No migration for existing routes. New lookup support requires SDK 2.9.0, a durable provider companion, a signed matching capability manifest, current authorization and explicitly configured browser origins. Import the standalone adapter from @bsv/overlay-express/output-lookup, or call configureOutputLookup before start. The legacy root loads the adapter lazily. One service binds each concrete base path; do not advertise unsupported profiles. Storage lifecycle and TLS, proxy deadlines and physical authentication capacity remain host responsibilities. Package publication and deployment remain separate authorized actions. The optional root-eviction-response entry requires middleware 2.3.0 and SDK 2.9.0. Capture the shared root revision before reading the complete response, list every disclosed advertisement and install current synchronous data/control access checks. All decision/access writers must share the durable gate. The transport companion resets stale candidates in full; it does not infer targets, mount root routes or retrofit existing lookup/cache/live/GASP paths. No existing route or stored-format migration.

entries.name: @bsv/overlay-topics
entries.summary: Advances the packed Overlay runtime dependency for the additive retained-admission history API. Existing package behavior and defaults remain unchanged; history retention is not enabled automatically.
entries.migration: None. The compatible dependency candidate does not change HTTP routes, topic/lookup interfaces, storage selection, or deployment configuration. Publication and deployment remain separate authorized actions.

entries.name: @bsv/paymail
entries.summary: Fixes the CommonJS build of the P2P signature and PaymailClient key helpers. The CommonJS build imported @bsv/sdk classes through bundler Node-mode interop, which bound each default import to the whole SDK module, so require() consumers failed at first use with ".default is not a constructor". SDK classes are now imported by name from the SDK barrels; the ESM build, public API and browser bundle size are unchanged.
entries.migration: None. ESM consumers are unaffected.

entries.name: @bsv/payment-express-middleware
entries.summary: Removes middleware payment-header size rejection so received payments are validated regardless of header size. Retains the deprecated maxPaymentHeaderBytes option as an ignored source-compatibility field. Atomic BEEF framing, canonical base64, derivation verification, pricing, wallet acceptance and atomic replay protection remain.
entries.migration: No BRC100 call, wire or wallet-data migration. maxPaymentHeaderBytes is now ignored, including existing explicit values: move transport policy to the HTTP server, CDN, proxy or WAF and remove the deprecated option. Validate the complete HTTP route for supported payment proofs. Published 2.1.8 is verified against protected release 36052862859 and its immutable source artifacts.

entries.name: @bsv/sdk
entries.summary: Adds opt-in BRC-192–199 protocol representations, exact encodings, capability selection, live lookup boundaries and closed proposal endpoint codecs while preserving all existing overlay APIs. Adds bounded local capability retention and original-contract revalidation for recovery. Adds bounded common service error envelopes and exact BRC-193 status mappings. Adds explicit AuthFetch automatic-payment opt-out, required mutual authentication and expected server identity controls while preserving existing defaults. Adds a bounded retained-contract BRC-193 HTTP client with authenticated selection binding, cancellation, unpaid errors and caller-owned durable cursor progression. WalletClient and the binary BRC-100 wire no longer reject every acquireCertificate issuance: result validation required the returned fields to equal the request's, but issuance sends plaintext values and the certificate comes back with each value encrypted. An issuance result is now bound to exactly the requested field names; a direct acquisition is still bound to its requested encrypted values exactly. Adds a separate portable BRC-197 exact locking-script, descriptor and revenue-state codec that authenticates the frozen executable before use. Adds separate six-route planning and funded transaction construction with exact mandatory outputs, integer revenue quanta, explicit retirement top-up, externally supplied seller and unanimous recipient transaction signatures, and final-layout binding. Protocol JSON maps explicitly construct own data fields while preserving accepted keys, null prototypes, property attributes and encodings. Adds bounded BRC-195/196 release representations, exact selected-policy binding and registered BRC-77 processor-attestation verification. Adds closed BRC-196 purchase endpoints, signed original-request terms and STEAK/POTATOES status, transaction, recipient and evidence bindings. Adds bounded BRC-195 protected-publication and paid-lookup representations, semantic publication digests and frozen quote, amount, recovery and purchased-output bindings. Adds bounded BRC-195 payment-header parsing, exact single BRC-29 funding-output inspection and proof-independent wallet operation identifiers. Adds bounded BRC-199 signed root request/result and status codecs, exact root/chain/requester and decision bindings, independent restoration bases and explicit new-request clock checks.
entries.migration: Existing exports, endpoints and lookup defaults remain unchanged. Select the new versioned profiles explicitly; the accompanying output-knowledge runtime provides durable application state above the SDK. Retained capability records are local replay material: persist them atomically with operations and independently enforce current authorization and operation deadlines. Use allowPayments: false for unpaid authenticated requests. Select requireMutualAuth to disable ordinary HTTP fallback, or expectedIdentityKey to additionally pin the canonical provider key before application dispatch; verify capability/profile bindings separately. Use HTTPS for confidentiality. Omitted controls preserve existing behavior. OutputLookupTransport is opt-in: persist the original opening before dispatch, and atomically commit each batch with its cursor before reading further. Full durable service/runtime integration is separate; no default legacy behavior changes. Import @bsv/sdk/script/templates/RevenueListing explicitly and supply the pinned program bytes; recognition does not establish lineage, currentness, valid spending or fulfillment. Existing root imports are unchanged. Opt into RevenueListingPlan/RevenueListingSpend only after domain lineage checks. Supply complete funding predecessors, preserve the planned BRC-100 two-phase layout, obtain raw ALL|FORKID signatures from explicit authorities, and verify the finalized transaction separately; the module never funds, signs or broadcasts by itself. Release-evidence helpers are opt-in: supply independently retained chain, transaction and release policy. Processor verification proves that selected processor signed the exact acceptance statement, not mining or delivery. Mined release still requires authenticated inclusion, selected-chain ancestry and a same-context commit check. No existing wire or stored-data migration. Purchase codecs preserve legacy STEAK and never fund or admit. Authenticate terms against the separately retained request and selected seller, persist them before construction, and supply the exact constructed transaction ID when checking reserved responses. Durable admission, domain/release eligibility and recipient usability remain separate checks. BRC-195 quote/status codecs require authenticated transport and an independently retained selected contract. They do not implement protected storage, wallet internalizeOnce, transaction/release eligibility or secret usability; legacy BRC-105 and lookup context are unchanged. Payment funding inspection requires an independently derived seller payment key, selected chain and retained quote; it does not establish Bitcoin acceptance, reserve an acquisition or internalize wallet value. Enforce total HTTP header limits and use a separate durable idempotent wallet adapter before acknowledging credit. Root-eviction helpers are opt-in and require independently authenticated context, the original signed request and retained evaluation policy. Check clocks only when accepting new requests; retained outcomes remain recoverable under current access policy. Evidence verification, local authority, durable tombstones and every serving/replay guard remain service obligations. Existing SHIP/SLAP, lookup and GASP behavior is unchanged.

entries.name: @bsv/simple
entries.summary: Corrects PushDrop self-derivation ownership, pins Message Box responses to the authenticated peer, hardens wallet, credential, DID, persistence, and transaction boundaries, preserves explicit offline migration identifiers and historical signature verification for pre-0.6 short certificate types while keeping new issuance, remote metadata, and wallet operations canonical 32-byte, and changes the generated server-wallet handler to require explicit authenticated action-level authorization. Shares one tested UTF-16 code-unit comparator across certificate signing and persisted field ordering, preserving historical ordering independently of locale.
entries.migration: Replace createServerWalletHandler() deployments with createServerWalletHandler({ authorize: async ({ action, headers }) => authenticatedSessionCanUseAction(headers, action) }). The callback must return literal true for each status, create, request, receive, balance, outputs, or reset action; omission now returns HTTP 403 for every action. Roll out the authentication layer and callback with the package, update anonymous probes or automation, and apply the same policy to every replica. Do not emulate the old public behavior with an unconditional authorize: () => true callback. Valid recipient derivations and authenticated Message Box peers remain supported; malformed, wrong-owner, or transaction-mutated flows now fail closed. New DID, CredentialSchema, and Certifier records use canonical 32-byte types. Current SDK wallet methods reject historical short types, so do not put migration aliases in wallet list, acquire, prove, or relinquish calls. Export affected records through the storage version that created them, authenticate them offline against the exact locally configured identifier, and reissue/import canonical replacements; no legacy certificate is rewritten automatically. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/. The internal comparator consolidation requires no migration and is included in the existing unpublished 0.6.0 candidate.

entries.name: @bsv/templates
entries.summary: Fixes the CommonJS build so require('@bsv/templates') consumers can construct Mandala, MultiPushDrop, OpReturn, P2MSKH and R1K1Wallet scripts again (issue #571). The CommonJS build imported @bsv/sdk classes through bundler Node-mode interop, which bound each default import to the whole SDK module, so require() consumers failed at first use with ".default is not a constructor". SDK classes are now imported by name from the SDK barrels; the ESM build, public API and browser bundle size are unchanged.
entries.migration: None. CommonJS consumers that patched 1.10.2 locally can drop the patch after upgrading to 1.10.3; ESM consumers are unaffected.

entries.name: @bsv/teranode-listener
entries.summary: Adds optional bounded decoding for Teranode's two-layer JSON message envelope and typed topic payload interfaces. Hardens the network boundary with canonical PNET, multiaddr, topic, configuration, callback, and numeric validation; immutable caller-owned inputs; exact runtime controls; coalesced retry-safe lifecycle transitions; and a working DHT-disable control. Replaces the internal placeholder subtree hash with the canonical Bitcoin Merkle root and verifies exact uint64 values, dimensions, totals, conflicts, framing, and resource ceilings before accepting serialized subtree state. Refreshes the compatible libp2p dependency set while retaining the imported source's hash-pinned MIT provenance and notices.
entries.migration: No API migration is required for valid consumers: raw callbacks remain the default and decoding is opt-in with decodeMessages: true. Configuration arrays and callbacks are snapshotted at construction, boolean controls must be literal booleans, and malformed or duplicate topics, addresses, keys, and unsupported properties now fail closed. usePrivateDHT: false now actually omits the DHT service. The published mainnet PNET value is transport compatibility data, not a publisher credential; decoded sender and payload fields remain untrusted and security-critical claims require independent validation. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package.

entries.name: @bsv/verifast
entries.summary: Hardens JavaScript, worker, and WebAssembly verification boundaries with exact network and height validation, literal consensus verdicts, uint32 flags, dense bounded byte and signature inputs, bounded batches, exact verdict shapes, and deterministic preload and disposal lifecycle handling.
entries.migration: Valid typed verification calls and worker protocols remain compatible. Custom module factories and WASM adapters must return the exact documented binary and boolean shapes; coercive network, height, flag, byte, batch, verdict, lifecycle, or disposed-instance values now fail closed. Keep THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with every JavaScript and WebAssembly distribution.

entries.name: @bsv/wallet-helper
entries.summary: Corrects caller-owned bilateral address derivation and hardens address generation, transaction building, prevout binding, P2PKH, Ordinal, OrdLock, preimage, sighash, OP_RETURN, script, amount, output, and final-wallet-transaction validation.
entries.migration: getAddress now derives with forSelf: true and returns the caller-owned side of the bilateral relationship. Applications that stored or coordinated the previous peer-owned result must regenerate and exchange the corrected address before sending value. Amount must be an integer from 1 through 1,000 and counterparties must be valid public keys. Valid canonical transaction-builder flows remain supported; malformed, ambiguous, or wallet-mutated results now fail closed. Distributors must retain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and LICENSES/ with the package.

entries.name: @bsv/wallet-relay
entries.summary: Adds the strict package contract and preserves wallet RPC, encrypted relay payloads, signatures, and transaction bytes across number-array, Uint8Array, Buffer, and historical numeric-key JSON runtimes. Standardizes first-party author metadata on the current BSV Association name. Enforces signed pairing metadata before relay resolution, requires HTTPS outside loopback development for pairing origins and directly configured relay APIs, and rejects privileged wallet methods when no explicit approval callback is configured. Retains portable wallet RPC byte handling and the strict package contract. Tolerates two missed heartbeat pongs by default and adds close diagnostics whose callback failures cannot interrupt disconnect cleanup. Hardens both wallet-RPC trust boundaries with exact argument and security-sensitive result validation; serializes sequence acceptance and outbound encryption; prevents stale mobile lifecycle work, reconnect identity squatting, active-socket authorization after expiry, and shutdown races; makes session lifetime absolute; and bounds concurrent wallet requests, log retention, response bodies, session capacity, and creation rate. Restricts active QR artifacts, pairing-URI structure, and scaffold output paths; adds no-store bearer-response policy, constant-time desktop-token checks, safe browser WebSocket subprotocol authentication, deterministic relay teardown, fail-closed callback containment, strict scaffold request parsing, and corrected wallet-authentication UI semantics.
entries.migration: Enable signed QR codes and distribute only HTTPS pairing origins and relay API URLs. Root-relative API paths and loopback HTTP remain supported. Configure onApprovalRequired for every method not deliberately listed in autoApproveMethods; unsigned pairing URIs and implicit approval are no longer accepted. Existing relay sessions, custom RPC method names, and supported wallet RPC byte encodings remain valid, and host applications continue to provide their matching Express runtime and type graph. Version 0.5 defaults to two missed pongs; set maxMissedHeartbeats to 1 to retain the prior heartbeat policy. Heartbeat intervals must fit the Node timer range. Preserve Cache-Control: no-store at proxies, prefer the stable bsv-wallet-relay plus token WebSocket subprotocols over the legacy token query parameter, and configure edge rate limiting in addition to the bounded in-process defaults. The 24-hour connected-session lifetime no longer renews on reconnect, malformed wallet calls fail with code 400, and WalletRelayClient retains at most 100 log entries unless maxLogEntries is configured. The QR remains a short-lived bearer invitation: keep it private and require explicit operation approval. Relay envelopes, cryptographic framing, and wallet RPC encodings remain unchanged.

entries.name: @bsv/wallet-toolbox
entries.summary: WalletPermissionsManager retires signed no-send ownership and reference aliases after createAction or signAction reports sending or unproven, including sendWith-only calls and successful members of an undelayed review error. Failed or unreported actions retain their originator binding for retry or abort. Cleanup visits only the retired transaction's references and preserves aliases reused by newer actions. Optional local SQLite controllers additionally retain exact two-phase noSend allocation/signing state and atomically reconcile one BRC-29 funding output with wallet ownership, deferred monitor work and a durable receipt. The new deep imports do not add root exports or BRC-100 RPC methods.
entries.migration: For ordinary callers, no public API, wire, database, or consumer migration is required. Pending no-send actions and retryable failures retain the same originator-bound abort behavior; positively queued or broadcast actions no longer retain session ownership records. Recovery adoption requires SDK 2.9.0, explicit auxiliary schema installation in the active local SQLite wallet, stable operation IDs and a committed workspace. Reopen retained state after restart; never silently reinstall a missing journal. These journals are outside legacy entity snapshots, BRC-38/39 export, ordinary sync, IndexedDB and remote providers. Back up the whole consistent wallet database plus keys and test restoration. For rollback, stop new adoption and reconcile outstanding operations with the original controller before removing it; preserve journals and keys. Local receipts do not establish quote-time capacity, settlement, domain authority or protected delivery.

entries.name: @bsv/wallet-toolbox-client
entries.summary: WalletPermissionsManager retires signed no-send ownership and reference aliases after createAction or signAction reports sending or unproven, including sendWith-only calls and successful members of an undelayed review error. Failed or unreported actions retain their originator binding for retry or abort. Cleanup visits only the retired transaction's references and preserves aliases reused by newer actions. The coordinated 2.15.0 candidate retains the browser/mobile-safe API while core adds optional Node SQLite recovery through separate deep imports. Installing this wrapper does not expose those local recovery controllers or storage adapters.
entries.migration: For ordinary callers, no public API, wire, database, or consumer migration is required. Pending no-send actions and retryable failures retain the same originator-bound abort behavior; positively queued or broadcast actions no longer retain session ownership records. Existing SDK peer ranges and browser/mobile/remote provider capabilities remain unchanged. The core local SQLite recovery guides do not grant IndexedDB, mobile or remote recovery guarantees. Do not replace durable core recovery with wrapper retries or entity-only backups; preserve any core journals and keys through rollback.

entries.name: @bsv/output-knowledge
entries.summary: Initial application output knowledge reference runtime, interchangeable durable journals, scoped provider currentness, durable expiry and bounded source equivocation quarantine. Adds an optional installed-proposal policy entry with author-document signature, revision and exact finalization relation checks. Adds pure proposal lifecycle plans for durable reservation, expiry and terminal admission outcomes. Adds bounded Memory and SQLite proposal journals with atomic lifecycle events, admission jobs, cross-channel operation claims and crash recovery. Adds atomic local recovery context and reserved terminal-receipt capacity with shared SQLite limit sealing. Binds retained proposal contracts to exact installed policies and exposes indexed atomic record/context reads. Adds durable proposal service orchestration with current access checks, original contract recovery, receipt/response capacity preflight and a concrete bounded SDK evidence adapter. Adds original evidence-context retention in versioned reservations and a compatible admission recovery argument. Adds optional bounded operation state stores with immutable configuration, atomic compare-and-swap, exact immediate-write recovery and Memory, SQLite and IndexedDB adapters. Adds an optional durable BRC-193 live lookup source with retained opening identity, bounded capture-before-delivery, exact core-receipt cursor gates, progressive snapshot/live ingestion, generation fencing and durable continuity resets. Adds a separate bounded full-history revenue-listing verifier with seller-authorized genesis, collect-before-resolve BEEF assembly, both merge parents and explicit covenant execution even for mined transitions. Adds an optional dedicated revenue-listing authority port and software-key implementation that use the same explicit authority identity for seller-authorized genesis and covenant transaction signatures. Adds a separate bounded SQLite root-advertisement journal with signed immutable request retention, independent suppression/restoration bases, frozen action attribution, root-authorized currentness assessments, durable projection intents and a shared cross-process final synchronous enqueue gate. Adds a separate current-format SHIP/SLAP evidence adapter with advertiser authentication, exact consuming-transaction verification and selected-ancestry placement. Adds optional root commit observations with the clock, access, installed policy and external context checked after acquiring the durable gate. Adds portable exact root capability selection and original-manifest recovery with stricter advertised/profile bounds. Adds opt-in atomic original-capability/request retention, narrower result reservations and an explicit transactional root journal format1-to2 upgrade with old-connection fencing. Adds an opt-in Node maintenance companion for bounded pending scans and client-independent expiry under the existing journal gate. Adds optional checked original-contract recovery by durable request digest for installed root workers.
entries.migration: New opt-in package above the SDK. Preserve wallet custody and explicit action authorization; do not infer spending from source membership changes. New journals seal configured currentness rules in local frame v3 with canonical assessment ordering. Existing v1/v2 journals retain their encoding and replay behavior when read or extended. Adopting v3 for an older journal or changing policies requires a new namespace; retain the old journal for audit and recovery. Body-only proposal journal entries retain their bytes and retry keys. Upgrade all SQLite proposal writers before relying on reserved completion capacity; capacity limits are sealed, and older pending jobs do not gain retroactive guarantees. ProposalService requires durable context/capacity storage, an authenticated transport, a current host access policy and idempotent durable topic admission. SDKProposalEvidence verifies exact BEEF/Script against an installed immutable chain view; it does not replace topic rules or establish unspentness. Legacy proposal-service/1 records remain readable; rich evidence reservations use local proposal-service/2, so upgrade readers before writing v2. Context-required admission cannot synthesize missing legacy material. Reservation verification and actual durable topic assessment remain distinct. Import workflow control storage from ./operations or ./operations/sqlite. These local CAS cells do not replace receipt journals or validate protocol transitions. Use explicit create only for new workflow identities; recover existing storage with open, and treat absence as lost state. Existing exports and journal formats remain unchanged. Import the live adapter from ./sources/live-lookup. Create its durable control cell once before network I/O, recover that exact cell after restart, and reuse the source instance across cancelled or uncertain connection attempts. Its local control format is output-live-lookup-source/1. Lost continuity requires an explicit new source generation; a local reset never manufactures a successful cursor or Bitcoin spend. Existing finite adapters and their browser entry are unchanged. Import the optional revenue-listing entry explicitly and supply the authenticated fixed program plus an installed immutable chain view. Its historical verdict does not establish asset authority, currentness, acquisition association or private fulfillment. No existing root export, wire format or journal migration. The optional revenue-listing authority port requires explicit dedicated key custody and installed consent policy; it never extracts a wallet funding root key or substitutes BRC-100 derived identities. Its signature checks do not establish full-transaction validity, lineage or fulfillment, and it introduces no existing stored-format migration. Root storage is opt-in through root-eviction types and root-eviction/sqlite. Explicit creation uses a new database file; recovery never creates missing state or changes its sealed identity, chain or capacities. All service instances and serving adapters must share the same durable gate. The journal does not install requester authority, validate advertisement BEEF/Script, implement broader bans or expiry scheduling, or mount HTTP handlers. Current authorization, evidence policy, index integration and final middleware enqueue qualification remain service responsibilities; do not advertise the full BRC-199 profile from this component alone. Import SDKRootEvictionEvidence from root-eviction/evidence with an installed immutable chain resolver and owned verification context. Its verified facts do not authorize suppression/restoration or establish currentness, and operator references are not fetched or automatically authorized. No existing wire or stored-format migration. Existing deterministic root methods and stored format remain unchanged. The optional RootEvictionCheckedStorage companion requires synchronous trusted clock/access/context callbacks that share the same physical gate or an independently coherent local port. Retain the returned observed head through signing and recheck it at final enqueue. These methods do not install network authentication, chain currentness or operator policy. RootEvictionContracts requires the original retained selector on recovery. Its record must be persisted atomically with first intake; the portable helper does not itself store that record; use the optional coordinated journal for atomic intake. RootEvictionCoordinatedStorage is an optional companion. Existing configurations retain exact root-eviction/1 behavior. New coordination configurations use root-eviction/2 and a sealed bounded original-contract byte capacity; upgrade existing files only through upgradeCoordination with the same root, chain and prior capacities. Already-open old connections fail after upgrade. Preserve backups and all history; missing legacy selections remain unavailable and cannot be invented from current discovery. HTTP, broader local bans, scheduling and all serving adapters remain separate requirements. SQLiteRootEvictionMaintenance opens an existing root journal with its exact sealed configuration; no new format or implicit creation. Install synchronous root-maintenance authorization and a trusted clock. Schedule bounded startup and periodic scan passes, restarting without a cursor at each pass end. Maintenance does not grant requester status access, process peer decisions or restore eligibility. RootEvictionRecoveryStorage preserves existing interfaces and formats. Authorize its worker guard independently of requester status access; missing original selections remain unavailable. Run maintenance expiry even when current chain/context checks prevent richer recovery.
